notes: Compare results only within the same provider, ranking, edition and scope. QS and THE use different methodologies; this guide does not combine them into a single score.
Overall university rankings and subject rankings are separate measures. The subject results below describe institutional subject areas, not EU-HEM or a particular host school.
The 2027 overall editions were available by the review date. Subject results shown here are from the 2026 edition. Each row retains its own edition year.

universities.summary: Get to know the university behind your Bologna studies: the Department of Economics, its health policy research, the buildings around Scaravilli, and the services that support your academic life.

about.text: The University of Bologna traces its origins to the medieval Studium, with 1088 used as its conventional foundation date. Its history connects the development of university education with the city itself. Exploring that heritage adds context to studying in Bologna, from its scholarly traditions to the university collections and buildings woven into the urban landscape.

For EU-HEM students, the relevant academic home is the Department of Economics, known as DSE. Its research extends across health, inequality, public policy and other areas of economics. The university's dedicated programme website brings together the course structure, timetable, examinations and faculty information you will use during your studies.

faq.q: Is the department address also my classroom?
faq.a: A department address is a reference point. Your official timetable identifies the location for each class, which can vary between courses. Check it before travelling.

faq.q: What is the difference between Studenti Online and Virtuale?
faq.a: Studenti Online is the student administration portal. Virtuale is the platform the programme links for teaching materials. You may need both during the same week for different tasks.

faq.q: Where can I check exams on my phone?
faq.a: The official myUniBo app supports exam bookings, grades, session locations and related messages. Download it through the university's app page and sign in with your university account.

faq.q: Can I use library resources away from campus?
faq.a: The university provides EZproxy for remote access to restricted electronic resources. Follow the library's instructions; access to a particular item depends on the resource and your university entitlement.

faq.q: How can I learn Italian alongside EU-HEM?
faq.a: Start with CLA's course catalogue. It lists different Italian pathways and self-study options, each with its own level and audience. Check registration details rather than assuming every course is open to all students.

faq.q: Where should I take an international student administration question?
faq.a: Use UniBo's international contact directory. It separates general arrival guidance from procedures such as submission of foreign qualifications and completion of matriculation, helping you reach the correct office.

faq.q: Which platform should I use for which task?
faq.a: Use Virtuale for teaching material, Studenti Online for administration, and AlmaEsami for exam registration. Check the relevant platform rather than assuming an action in one updates the others.

faq.q: How can I find a place for group study?
faq.a: Explore library locations and SPEIS room booking early. For group work, check whether a particular space supports discussion and requires a reservation.

universities.name: University of Oslo
universities.tagline: Health economics, policy and management within a medical faculty
universities.summary: Founded in 1811, Norway's oldest university brings EU-HEM into a multidisciplinary environment connecting economics, health services and public policy.

about.text: The University of Oslo combines education and research with science communication and innovation. Its academic community spans disciplines, while university museums and public events connect knowledge with the wider city.

EU-HEM is offered through the Department of Health Management and Health Economics, known as HELED. Its researchers include economists, political scientists and physicians, with projects developed in collaboration with health-service professionals.

highlights.title: A health-services perspective
highlights.text: Explore how economics, policy and management connect with the organisation and quality of care.

highlights.title: Research across disciplines
highlights.text: University initiatives connect health and life sciences with wider environmental and societal questions.

highlights.title: Support for academic work

academic.unit: Department of Health Management and Health Economics · HELED
academic.text: HELED sits within the Institute of Health and Society in the Faculty of Medicine. Its teaching and research cover health economics, health policy, health systems, quality of care and management. Use the dedicated European Master programme page for EU-HEM information; the department also lists a separate Health Economics, Policy and Management degree.

faq.q: Which Oslo programme page should I use for EU-HEM?
faq.a: Use the European Master in Health Economics and Management page. HELED also offers a separately named Health Economics, Policy and Management degree, so check the programme title before following instructions.

faq.q: How do Studentweb, Canvas and My Studies differ?
faq.a: Studentweb handles registration and student administration. Canvas contains teaching materials, assignments and course communication. My Studies brings together your personal schedule, messages and useful service shortcuts.

faq.q: Are all my classes at the HELED address?
faq.a: Use the department address for its location. Check My Studies and programme messages for each teaching session's location and any changes to your schedule.

faq.q: What should I do if I cannot activate my account?
faq.a: Check the official international-student account guide and ensure your recorded phone number includes the country code. Contact IT Help if you still cannot obtain or use your credentials.

faq.q: Where can I get help with literature and academic writing?
faq.a: Start with the University Library's search and referencing support. Its Academic Writing Centre offers help discussing ideas and drafts; check the current consultation arrangements on the library website.

faq.q: Who can help with international student practicalities?
faq.a: Knutepunktet is UiO's International Student Reception. Its page separates contact routes for applicants and current students and links guidance on registration, arrival matters and social activities.

faq.q: How can I get to know the academic setting?
faq.a: Read the consortium's HELED introduction and identify how your interests connect with economics, health services or organisational research. Prepare specific questions for the programme team.

faq.q: Are registration and course learning handled in the same place?
faq.a: Use the Studentweb registration guidance and Canvas learning guidance for their distinct purposes. Confirm the steps that apply to your joint-degree status with the programme office.

universities.name: Erasmus University Rotterdam
universities.tagline: Health economics and policy in a multidisciplinary research environment.
universities.summary: Erasmus University Rotterdam brings together a long economics tradition with medicine and the social sciences. EU-HEM is hosted by Erasmus School of Health Policy & Management, with Campus Woudestein as its Rotterdam study setting.

about.text: Erasmus University’s roots go back to the Netherlands School of Commerce, established in 1913 with support from Rotterdam’s business community. The university took its present form in 1973, when the Netherlands School of Economics and the Medical Faculty Rotterdam merged. It is named after the humanist Desiderius Erasmus.

The Rotterdam EU-HEM experience sits within Erasmus School of Health Policy & Management (ESHPM). Its academic environment connects economics, law, organisational science and other disciplines with healthcare. For students, that creates useful opportunities to explore how evidence informs decisions about care, resources and health systems.

Woudestein is a shared university campus with study facilities, student services and spaces for activities beyond your programme. The library, sports facilities, cultural programme and student associations are useful starting points for building a routine and meeting people across disciplines.

faq.q: Which school hosts EU-HEM in Rotterdam?
faq.a: EU-HEM is hosted by Erasmus School of Health Policy & Management (ESHPM). Its official programme page lists Campus Woudestein as the location.

faq.q: Are all my classes in the Bayle building?
faq.a: Bayle is ESHPM’s visiting address. Your teaching room is determined by the current timetable and programme instructions; check the building code before travelling.

faq.q: How do MyEUR, Canvas and OSIRIS differ?
faq.a: MyEUR is the student intranet; Canvas supports course learning and materials; OSIRIS handles study records and administration. Follow EU-HEM instructions for registration and assessment.

faq.q: Can I read library articles away from campus?
faq.a: Start from the library website and use your ERNA account when prompted. Access depends on your account and the university’s licence for the resource.

faq.q: Where should I go with a study or personal concern?
faq.a: ESHPM study advisers are the first contact for study-related questions. The university support directory also helps you find counsellors, psychologists and disability support.

faq.q: What if I cannot access my EUR systems?
faq.a: Use the IT Services guidance for account and technical problems. If you cannot enter MyEUR, the public Erasmus Student Service Centre page provides contact routes for assistance.

faq.q: Where can I study quietly or work with a group?
faq.a: The library describes East as a quiet area and West as suitable for discussion and working together. Review the reservation instructions and check in when required.

faq.q: Where should I check academic and examination rules?
faq.a: ESHPM publishes programme-specific Teaching and Examination Regulations. Use the version that applies to your programme and year, and ask an advisor when a rule is unclear.

universities.name: MCI | The Entrepreneurial School
universities.tagline: Applied health management in an entrepreneurial academic community.
universities.summary: MCI combines higher education with applied research, business and public-sector practice. Its EU-HEM community connects healthcare management with a wider environment of social innovation, entrepreneurship and international study in Innsbruck.

about.text: Established in 1995/96, Management Center Innsbruck developed around a practical approach to higher education. Today, MCI describes its model as connecting academic teaching, applied research, knowledge transfer and entrepreneurship. Its programmes span management and society as well as technology and life sciences.

For a health economics and management student, this creates several routes beyond the classroom: exploring social and health research, discussing a business idea, developing professional skills or joining international activities. MCI operates its own programmes and student platforms, alongside partnerships with other institutions in Innsbruck.

highlights.title: Connections with practice
highlights.text: MCI emphasises cooperation with organisations and the application of research. Use the programme page to explore its learning goals and current professional connections.

academic.text: MCI’s EU-HEM programme page is the starting point for its curriculum, learning goals and programme office. Teaching connects healthcare challenges with management, economics and international perspectives. Use your cohort’s programme instructions to confirm module arrangements, assessment and thesis requirements.

faq.q: Is MCI the University of Innsbruck?
faq.a: MCI is the EU-HEM partner in Innsbruck and has its own programmes and student systems. It collaborates with other local institutions, including through the University and State Library of Tyrol.

faq.q: Where will my classes take place?
faq.a: MCI has several locations. Use your current timetable and the programme office’s instructions to identify the correct building and room.

faq.q: What is the difference between myMCI and Sakai?
faq.a: myMCI covers course information, examinations and administrative processes. Sakai supports course materials, assignments and digital collaboration.

faq.q: Can I use the University and State Library of Tyrol?
faq.a: MCI’s library cooperation includes ULB services. Follow the current student-card activation instructions; access to the two institutions’ electronic collections has different conditions.

faq.q: Can I take German alongside EU-HEM?
faq.a: Explore the Language Center’s German courses and registration dates. Ask about places, fees and any recognition within your programme before booking.

faq.q: Who should I contact for help?
faq.a: Use the EU-HEM programme office for academic arrangements, Student Support for organisational questions and the IT Helpdesk for digital access. Their official pages keep the current contact details.

faq.q: Is ULB access the same as MCI online-library access?
faq.a: MCI documents activation of the student card for ULB services through myMCI. Its own online collection supports remote access; University of Innsbruck online-resource access has different restrictions.

faq.q: Where can I find support for reference management?
faq.a: Explore MCI's Citavi licence guidance and library training when setting up your first written assignment. Follow the academic standards that apply to your programme.
